QF.id: IV Strategies Using Interest Rate Derivatives_26

question.text: A trader enters a long straddle on a GOI bond option at strike Rs. 96, paying Rs. 0.80 for the call and Rs. 0.70 for the put. The contract is on 2,000 bonds (Rs. 2,00,000 face value at Rs. 100). If the underlying GOI bond settles at Rs. 94.20, what is the total profit per contract in rupees?

explanation.text: The Logic: Exchange-traded interest rate options are currently on GOI dated securities with 2,000-bond lots (workbook pp. 152-153). For a long straddle, both premiums are recovered before profit (workbook pp. 174-175). Total premium per Rs. 100 = 0.80 + 0.70 = 1.50. At Rs. 94.20 the call expires worthless and the put payoff = 96 - 94.20 = 1.80 per Rs. 100. Net P&L per Rs. 100 = 1.80 - 1.50 = 0.30. Per contract = 0.30 x 2,000 = Rs. 600. The Trap: Rs. 3,600 ignores the premium paid (1.80 x 2,000). Rs. 1,200 doubles the answer. Rs. 2,400 uses an inconsistent multiplier. Note: The break-evens of a long straddle are strike minus or plus total premium (here, 94.50 and 97.50).
